title: North Carolina Utilities Commission Issues Order on Carbon Plan and Integrated Resource Plan

documents.text:
State of North Carolina
                                        Utilities Commission
                                              COMMISSIONERS
                                        William M. Brawley, Chairman
                               Floyd B. McKissick, Jr.    John W. Gajda
                               Tommy Tucker            Donald R. van der Vaart

                           NORTH CAROLINA UTILITIES COMMISSION

                                          PRESS RELEASE
    Release: Immediate                                  Contact: James West, General Counsel

    Date: November 16, 2026                             Phone: 919-733-3969

                     NORTH CAROLINA UTILITIES COMMISSION
          ISSUES ORDER ON CARBON PLAN AND INTEGRATED RESOURCE PLAN

Today’s unanimous1 and bipartisan Carbon Plan and Integrated Resource Plan (CPIRP)
order positions North Carolina for continued economic growth while balancing reliability,
resource adequacy, energy security, and cost. The Commission’s decision follows a
twelve-day expert witness hearing and five public witness hearings held across the State
and virtually. More than 600 people submitted consumer statements of position. Four
parties submitted system modeling evidence and 11 parties filed expert witness testimony.

The order approves a diverse set of near-term actions to meet growing electricity demand,
maintain reliability, and protect customers. Those actions include:

      •    Strategically extending certain coal-unit retirement dates beyond those approved
           in the Commission’s 2024 CPIRP Order and requiring Duke to file an updated coal
           retirement analysis with its next CPIRP;

      •    Extending through 2028 the authorization for up to $440 million in advanced
           nuclear development costs, preserving the option to develop either 600 MW of
           small modular reactors or approximately 1,117 MW of large light water reactor
           generation;

      •    Opening a dedicated new nuclear resources docket and convening a technical
           conference in 2027 to inform the Commission’s evaluation of reactor technology,



1
    Commissioner van der Vaart did not participate in the decision.
        costs, financing, execution risks, and customer protections before any decision to
       build a new nuclear plant;

   •   Authorizing Duke to develop and submit amendments to the Nuclear Regulatory
       Commission for two AP1000 units at the W.S. Lee site and revisions to the
       combined license application for two AP1000 units at the Shearon Harris site;

   •   Pursuing approximately 2,730 MW of new natural gas-fired combined-cycle
       generation and approximately 1,111 MW of additional combustion-turbine
       generation between 2030 and 2033;

   •   Procuring up to 2,300 MW of new solar resources to be placed in service between
       2032 and 2034;

   •   Requiring solar procurements to include customer-protection measures, including
       the volume adjustment mechanism, market depth adjustment mechanism, and an
       independent evaluator;

   •   Developing and procuring up to 2,700 MW of additional battery energy storage,
       bringing planned system battery storage to as much as 5,400 MW by 2034;

   •   Authorizing up to $55.6 million for near-term development of Bad Creek II,
       including activities to preserve federal energy tax credits and the option to place
       1,760 MW of pumped-storage hydropower in service by 2040; and

   •   Authorizing Duke to continue planning to achieve the 22% reserve margin by 2031.

The Commission recognizes the check-and-adjust nature of the biennial CPIRP process,
which allows it to respond to changing load forecasts, market conditions, technology
costs, and resource availability. Duke will submit its next proposed CPIRP in Fall 2027.

The complete order and record are available on the Commission’s website under Docket
No. E-100, Sub 207.



Raleigh, North Carolina –
